name_note: GTDB uses the new genus name Methanocatella; nearly all published work calls this archaeon Methanobrevibacter smithii.

sentences.text: Members of the genus Methanobrevibacter have been reclassified into eight novel genera, among them Methanocatella.

Methanobrevibacter smithii is described as a dominant member of the human gut microbiome, and a study characterised its enzyme ArmA as the first glycosyl hydrolase specific for archaeal peptidoglycan.
A study reported that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, but with distinct kinetics.
In a murine oral gavage model, a study reported that Methanobrevibacter smithii modulated mucosal immunity through innate and adaptive immune compartments.
